items.title: Earl King Interview, 1980-04-10
items.q: one of the, the, the first organ groups other than Bill Doggett I heard in, in America

ctx.x: We have a question about Jamie Booker, who's a studio pianist, and also recorded a number of records. I don't know if anyone's heard of him. He's a local pianist. I guess he wants to know what his contribution was, in the scene here in the world.

Booker is about one of the most underrated producers. You know him as a musician, but most people, they know of Booker as being the dynamic hens as he is. But Booker put a lot of, projected a lot of creative ideas into some of the music that's been going on around New Orleans. Even on some of my recordings, they played like, uh, uh, Mom and Papa and things like that. But Booker was originally a saxophone player, and he played very well. Most people don't know that. And, uh, uh, one of the, the, the first organ…
You know? But that's been one of the reasons why the president's companies came from out of town, because they didn't take it. Right.
